query: Which material can be used for improve the magnetocaloric properties, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Doping La(Fe,Si)13-based alloys with cobalt increases their magnetocaloric effect near room temperature by shifting the Curie temperature and strengthening the magnetic transition.
generation.intervention: Partial substitution of iron by cobalt in La(Fe,Si)13
generation.conditions: Alloys prepared by arc melting followed by heat treatment; varying Co concentration (e.g., 5–10 at.%) and magnetocaloric measurements under moderate fields near room temperature
generation.structural_mediator: Alteration of magnetic exchange interactions through cobalt substitution
generation.mechanism: Cobalt doping modifies magnetic ordering, thus tuning the Curie temperature and enhancing the magnetocaloric response around room temperature
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved magnetocaloric effect relative to undoped La(Fe,Si)13-based alloys, particularly in the targeted near-room-temperature range
generation.boundary: Optimal Co content and heat treatment must be determined; excessive doping or improper processing may reduce the magnetocaloric benefit
generation.uncertainty: Exact improvement magnitude is uncertain without direct empirical data

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize multiple La(Fe,Si)13−xCox specimens (with x in small increments), measure magnetization versus temperature under controlled fields, and compare their magnetocaloric effect to undoped samples over the same temperature ranges.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the cobalt-doped samples do not exhibit a measurable enhancement in magnetocaloric effect or shift in Curie temperature compared to the undoped baseline, or if any observed effects cannot be reproduced experimentally, the hypothesis would be falsified.
